title: Registration & Welcome Coffee
description: Collect your conference badge and programme booklet from the registration desk in the main foyer.

title: Opening Keynote: Reimagining Higher Education for the 21st Century
description: Professor Nkosi delivers the opening address exploring how emerging technologies are fundamentally reshaping the learning landscape in African universities, with reflections on institutional readiness and student equity.

title: Morning Tea & Networking
description: Light refreshments served in the exhibition foyer. Poster presentations open.

title: Designing for Inclusion: Universal Design for Learning in Large Lecture Halls
description: This session presents findings from a two-year UDL implementation study across engineering and health sciences faculties. Practical frameworks and student feedback data are shared.

title: AI-Assisted Feedback in Programming Courses: A Pilot Study
description: A report on using LLM-based tools to provide instant formative feedback to first-year computer science students. Results show a 22% improvement in assignment scores.

title: Decolonising the Curriculum: Case Studies from Social Sciences
description: Three faculty teams share their experiences redesigning undergraduate syllabi to centre African epistemologies. Includes discussion of institutional resistance and student responses.

title: Flipped Classroom Evidence: What Does the Data Actually Say?
description: A meta-analysis of 14 flipped classroom studies conducted at South African universities between 2019-2024. The presenter challenges some popular assumptions with uncomfortable data.

title: Building an AI Literacy Framework for Non-Technical Students
description: How do we prepare humanities and social science students to navigate an AI-mediated world? This session presents a competency framework piloted across three faculties.

title: Writing for Publication: Getting Your Research Into Journals
description: An intensive hands-on workshop covering academic writing structure, journal selection strategies, and responding to reviewer comments. Bring a draft abstract to work on.

title: Lunch Break
description: Lunch served in the main dining hall. Vegetarian and halaal options available. Poster session continues in foyer.

title: Student Voices: What Do Learners Actually Need from Technology?
description: A panel of five students from different universities discuss their lived experience of digital learning tools, hybrid attendance, and assessment anxiety. Facilitated open Q&A.

title: Rubric Design for Authentic Assessment in Professional Programmes
description: Moving beyond knowledge recall to assess graduate attributes. The presenter shares rubric templates developed collaboratively with industry partners in nursing and engineering.

title: ChatGPT in the Classroom: Threat or Teaching Tool?
description: A frank examination of generative AI in assessment contexts. This session covers detection limitations, academic integrity policies, and redesigning assessments to be AI-resilient.

title: Afternoon Tea
description: Refreshments in the foyer. Book signing with keynote speaker.

title: Service Learning as a Graduation Requirement: Lessons from Five Years
description: An honest evaluation of the mandatory service-learning programme introduced in 2019. What worked, what failed, and what the data says about graduate employability.

title: Morning Registration & Coffee
description: Day 2 registration and refreshments in the main foyer.

title: The Future of Assessment: Beyond the Exam Hall
description: A provocative keynote arguing that traditional examinations are structurally biased and proposing a portfolio-based alternative used successfully across NWU Faculty of Education.

title: Morning Tea
description: Refreshments and informal networking.

title: Work-Integrated Learning Partnerships: Building Sustainable Industry Links
description: How to create, maintain, and evaluate meaningful industry partnerships for WIL programmes. Three case studies from engineering, hospitality, and ICT are examined.

title: Building Institutional Chatbots for Student Support
description: A technical and pedagogical walkthrough of deploying a student support chatbot that handles queries about registration, fees, and academic rules. Lessons learned from 8 months of operation.

title: Ethics in Educational Research: Navigating Institutional Review
description: Common pitfalls in ethics applications and how to design studies that are both rigorous and respectful of participants. Includes discussion of community-based participatory research.

title: Peer Assessment at Scale: Tools and Trust
description: How do you make peer marking work in a class of 300 students? This session covers platform selection, calibration exercises, and addressing student concerns about fairness.

title: Extended Reality (XR) in Health Sciences Education
description: Early results from VR anatomy labs and AR clinical simulation tools introduced in the nursing and physiotherapy programmes. Cost-benefit analysis included.

title: Research Grant Writing: Crafting Proposals That Succeed
description: A practical workshop on identifying funding opportunities, writing compelling problem statements, and building a competitive budget. Participants complete a mock grant section.

title: Lunch Break
description: Lunch in the main dining hall.

title: Disability and Digital: Accessibility in Online Learning Environments
description: A cross-institutional panel examines screen reader compatibility, caption quality, and the gap between institutional accessibility policies and actual student experience.

title: Micro-credentials and the Changing Shape of Qualifications
description: Are stackable credentials a democratising force or a commodification of education? This session examines the evidence and South Africa policy landscape.

title: Data-Driven Teaching: Using LMS Analytics to Support Students at Risk
description: A practical guide to setting up early warning dashboards in Moodle and Blackboard. Real case data shows how intervention timing affects throughput rates.

title: Engaged Scholarship: When the University Goes to the Community
description: The third-day keynote challenges the traditional extractive model of academic research in favour of long-term community partnership. A deeply personal and evidence-rich address.

title: Morning Tea
description: Refreshments and networking.

title: Mentoring Junior Academics: Structural Support vs Individual Goodwill
description: A critical look at formal mentoring programmes. What makes them succeed? The presenter shares a mixed-methods study spanning 6 faculties and 3 years, with actionable recommendations.

title: Learning Management Systems Compared: Moodle vs Blackboard vs Canvas
description: A head-to-head comparison of the three most common LMS platforms used in South African institutions. Focus on accessibility, mobile experience, analytics capability and cost.

title: Measuring Research Impact Beyond Citation Counts
description: Altmetrics, societal impact frameworks, and community knowledge transfer. How should African academics measure contribution in a global ranking system built for Western institutions?

title: Teaching Large Classes: Strategies That Actually Work
description: Practical techniques for maintaining engagement and quality in classes of 500+ students. Includes polling tools, structured peer discussion, and assessment design. Bring your laptop.

title: Building Inclusive Online Video Content: Captioning and More
description: A step-by-step workshop on producing accessible lecture videos. Topics include auto-captioning accuracy, audio description, and low-bandwidth alternatives for rural students.

title: Lunch & Poster Judging
description: Lunch in the main dining hall. Poster prize announcement at 13:15.

title: Internationalisation of the Curriculum: Global Perspectives Without Losing Local Relevance
description: Four academic leaders discuss integrating global case studies and international partnerships while ensuring content remains meaningful for South African students and communities.

title: Student Mental Health and Academic Performance: What Faculty Can Do
description: Drawing on counselling data from 2021-2024 and faculty interviews, this session provides concrete classroom adjustments that reduce student anxiety without compromising standards.

title: Open Educational Resources: Building a Departmental OER Strategy
description: Why OER matters for African higher education equity and how to build a departmental strategy from scratch. Includes platform recommendations and copyright guidance.

title: Closing Keynote: What Does a Transformed University Actually Look Like?
description: A visionary and challenging closing address drawing together themes from the conference - equity, technology, community, and assessment - into a coherent vision for transformation.

title: Morning Tea
description: Final networking opportunity.

title: Portfolios as Assessment: Moving from Products to Processes
description: A practical guide to implementing e-portfolios across a faculty. The presenter shares technical setup on Mahara and the assessment rubrics developed with student input.

title: Artificial Intelligence Policy in Higher Education: Where Are We Now?
description: A policy landscape review of how South African and global institutions are responding to generative AI. Includes analysis of 22 published AI policies with common themes.

title: Participatory Action Research with Students: A Methodological Guide
description: Students as co-researchers rather than subjects. This session outlines a PAR methodology adapted for South African undergraduate contexts and shares three completed studies.

title: Designing Hybrid Assessment That Works for Both Cohorts
description: Practical frameworks for designing assessments that are equally fair and rigorous whether submitted digitally or in-person. Focus on equivalence without doubling workload.

title: From Pilot to Scale: Technology Adoption Lessons from the Classroom
description: What separates successful edtech pilots from those that never move beyond the enthusiast classroom? A framework for sustainable technology adoption in resource-constrained institutions.

title: Closing Lunch
description: Final conference lunch with prize ceremony for best paper and best poster.

title: Awards Ceremony & Closing Remarks
description: Presentation of the Best Paper Award and Best Poster Award followed by closing remarks and announcement of next year conference.
